responsibility: Performs HIR-level type checking for Rust bodies and expressions, turning HIR for functions, closures, coroutines, and other body-like items into fully inferred, adjusted, and diagnostics-backed `TypeckResults` for the rest of the compiler. At the crate root, `lib.rs` orchestrates this work by wiring query providers, creating the shared root checking state, constructing per-body checking contexts, dispatching body checking, and coordinating fallback and writeback. The core checking framework is split between `inherited`, which owns the shared inference context, fulfillment state, local bindings, deferred checks, and obligation registration for a root body, and `fn_ctxt`, which defines the per-function/body `FnCtxt` and uses it to drive expression and call checking, inference bookkeeping, divergence tracking, deferred validations, and many context-sensitive diagnostics. Body checking begins in `check`, which checks function and closure bodies against declared signatures, sets up return coercion, gathers locals, enforces well-formedness and `Sized` requirements, and validates special entry-point signatures, while `gather_locals` predeclares locals and pattern bindings with either annotated types or fresh inference variables. `expr` is the main expression checker, propagating `expectation` information downward, invoking specialized logic for calls, operators, matches, closures, casts, and places, recording inferred types and adjustments, and enforcing subtype or coercion requirements; `expectation` defines those downward type expectations and helpers for adapting them across control-flow joins and coercion points. The crate’s coercion and adjustment machinery is provided by `coercion` for subtype, reborrow, autoderef/autoref, pointer, and branch LUB coercions, by `autoderef` for constructing autoderef searches and converting them into adjustments and obligations, and by `demand` for enriching type mismatch and failed-coercion diagnostics with targeted labels and suggestions. Specialized expression forms are checked by dedicated modules: `callee` handles function, closure, overloaded `Fn*`, const/effect-checked, and illegal call expressions; `method` resolves methods and associated value items by probing inherent and trait candidates, confirming the chosen callee, diagnosing failures and ambiguities, and issuing edition-compatibility lints; `op` handles unary, binary, and assignment operators, including overloaded trait-based operators; `place_op` handles overloaded or builtin dereference and indexing in place contexts; `cast` classifies and validates Rust casts and defers unresolved cases until enough type information is known; `intrinsicck` performs HIR-side layout-aware intrinsic checking, especially `transmute`; `closure` derives or infers closure and coroutine signatures and kinds, constructs their types, checks nested bodies, and extracts async/future output information; and `_match` checks `match`/`if` branching forms, including scrutinee and arm patterns, guards, divergence, branch coercion, and arm-type diagnostics. Pattern and place analysis are handled by `pat`, which type-checks patterns, match ergonomics, bindings, and destructuring, and by `mem_categorization`, which translates expressions and patterns into typed memory `Place` structures used by later move/borrow-sensitive analyses. Those analyses are then built in `expr_use_visitor`, which classifies uses such as moves, copies, borrows, mutations, bindings, and fake reads, and in `upvar`, which uses that information to infer closure capture kinds and precision, record captures, resolve deferred closure-call information, and emit capture-related edition diagnostics. Coroutine/generator support is extended by `generator_interior`, which computes interior types by combining suspension-point liveness with drop-range analysis to determine which values live across yields and to emit unresolved-type and `must_not_suspend` diagnostics. Temporary and control-flow semantics are modeled by `rvalue_scopes`, which computes rvalue lifetime extensions, and `diverges`, which defines the divergence/reachability model propagated during expression, branch, and body checking. After primary inference, `fallback` assigns defaults to unresolved integer, float, and diverging type variables, performs additional solving, and prepares never-type fallback diagnostics and related lint context, and `writeback` then resolves remaining inference variables, normalizes and erases regions from body-local types, adjustments, and capture information, and stores finalized immutable `TypeckResults`. Throughout the crate, `errors` centralizes the structured diagnostics and lint payload types used by these checkers so that HIR type-checking failures are reported consistently. Overall, `rustc_hir_typeck` is the compiler component that checks the types of HIR bodies, resolves calls, methods, patterns, operators, closures, and generators, manages local inference and coercions, performs body-local analyses needed for captures and suspension, and commits the completed type-checking results and diagnostics that later compiler stages rely on.
